subject: Mutual Action Plan: technical evaluation milestones & model shortlist (HealthGrid)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthgrid.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-07T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo — MAP draft: technical evaluation milestone ideas

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo time today. Per our call, I’m attaching a first-pass MAP sheet with the technical-eval milestone broken out so we have clear owners and acceptance criteria. High-level summary below and a few clarifying questions.

Quick MAP highlights (technical milestone):
- Milestone: Technical evaluation (owner: HealthGrid + Redwood SE)
  - Subtasks: benchmark harness, data/seed prompts, latency/cost targets, model shortlist, regression checks
  - Target close for milestone: 2026-09-30 (goal for overall MAP close: 2026-10-14)
- Success criteria (benchmark): p95 latency <= 150ms for 256-token responses under our simulated concurrency; token cost target <= $0.30 per 1k tokens for steady-state traffic; quality pass-rate >= 92% on your clinical extraction eval set
- Model shortlist (initial): Redwood-Refined-2-13B (quantized), Mistral-7B-v2, Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized) — we’ll include a 70B candidate only if latency/cost tradeoffs are acceptable

Dependencies / asks for HealthGrid:
- Sample prompt sets and 3 representative payloads (anonymized) by 2026-09-10
- Access to a staging endpoint for smoke tests or a Docker image of the harness if you prefer local run
- Confirm regulatory constraints for on-prem testing (PHI handling) — will that require Private deployment?

Attachments: HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP sheet, milestones tab), latency-benchmark-specs.md (benchmark harness spec).

Can you confirm owners on your side for the benchmark (platform lead + clinical SME) and whether the 9/30 milestone is realistic? If you prefer different thresholds for latency/cost, say now and we’ll iterate.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Rafael onto the timeline/ops details once we have the owners.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

---
Attachment: HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: latency-benchmark-specs.md (text spec stub)

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@healthgrid.com
Date: 2026-09-07T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo — MAP draft: technical evaluation milestone ideas

Thanks Karthik — appreciated the clear recap. A few quick notes from our side: we like the proposed structure and the 9/30 target feels achievable with caveats below.

Clarifying items / comments
- Owners: I’ll own the program lead; platform@healthgrid will provide the infra owner (TBD: Carlos from our infra). Clinical SME will be Dr. Priya Rao (cc’ing separately).
- Data: we can provide two sanitized examples and one redacted real payload by 2026-09-09. Will that be enough for the initial quality runs?
- PHI/on-prem: we need to confirm with security whether a Private deployment is required for any test data that contains PHI. Today, we plan to run initial microbenchmarks on a non-PHI sample in your hosted environment. If PHI becomes necessary, we’ll discuss Private.
- Success criteria: the quality pass-rate definition — is that your automated metric (F1/exact-match) or do you want a combined score? We prefer a single primary metric we can track.

Requests
- Can you add a row in the MAP with a short description for each model candidate’s expected tradeoffs (latency vs. accuracy vs. cost)? That will help our procurement.
- Please confirm whether the latency target is measured p95 per-request (end-to-end) or server-side token generation time.

We’ll review the attachments and confirm owners by end of day 9/8.

-Emily
Emily Zhang
Director, Product & Integrations | HealthGrid
emily.zhang@healthgrid.com

---
Note: Dr. Priya Rao will be looped in by 9/8 for clinical acceptance criteria.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthgrid.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-08T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo — MAP draft: technical evaluation milestone ideas

Emily — great, thanks for the fast turn. Quick answers inline and an updated mini-roadmap below.

Inline:
- Data: two sanitized and one redacted sample is sufficient for an initial pass. We’ll include a smoke harness that runs the 3 samples and reports the quality metric.
- PHI: understood. We’ll treat the first hosted run as non-PHI. If you need PHI testing, we’ll scope Private deployment steps (time approx 2–3 weeks for on-prem/hardened path).
- Quality metric: propose we use an F1-based primary metric (clinical extraction F1) and publish an exact-match secondary metric. We’ll show both in the run dashboard.
- Latency: measure p95 end-to-end request time (client to response complete) to reflect your real UX. Server-side token gen will be captured too but used for debugging.

Updated technical-eval mini-roadmap (owners + dates):
- 2026-09-09: HealthGrid supplies samples + confirm owners (Emily/Platform/Carlos/Dr. Priya) — owner: HealthGrid
- 2026-09-12: Redwood provides benchmark harness + model-tradeoff writeup (owner: Karthik/Marissa)
- 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-22: Benchmark runs (Redwood infra + HealthGrid staging) (owner: Redwood SE + HealthGrid infra)
- 2026-09-24: Internal quality readout + anomaly triage (owner: HealthGrid clinical + Redwood SE)
- 2026-09-30: Milestone decision (pass/fail/iterate) and recommendation for production path (owner: joint)

Model-tradeoff writeup: Rafael will attach an initial sheet comparing expected latency, cost, and accuracy for the shortlisted models (we’ll include per-1k-token cost estimates and quantization options).

Next steps: Rafael / Marissa — can you draft the tradeoff sheet and a short benchmark-run checklist by EOD 9/10? I’ll update the MAP sheet with the rows Emily requested.

Karthik

---
Attachment: latency-benchmark-specs.md (updated to include p95 end-to-end definition)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthgrid.com>, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-09T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — model tradeoffs sheet and checklist

Adding the tradeoff snapshot and checklist (summary below). I attached a draft spreadsheet to the MAP.

Tradeoff snapshot (draft):
- Redwood-Refined-2-13B (quantized int4) — expected p95 ~110–140ms (single-region), estimated cost $0.18–0.25 per 1k tokens, accuracy: high on extraction (baseline pass-rate 94% on our clinical set)
- Mistral-7B-v2 (float16) — expected p95 ~90–120ms, estimated cost $0.12–0.20 per 1k tokens, accuracy: slightly lower on few-shot clinical extraction (baseline 89%)
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8 quant) — expected p95 ~130–170ms, estimated cost $0.10–0.18 per 1k tokens, accuracy: 90% baseline
- 70B candidate (experimental) — p95 >200ms, cost >$0.6 per 1k tokens; include only if cost/latency tolerances are relaxed

Benchmark checklist (short):
- Confirm sample set + acceptance metric (F1 primary)
- Run harness with 3 sample payloads at 1, 5, 10 concurrent users
- Capture p50/p95/p99, token-cost estimate, and quality metrics per model
- Produce a one-page readout with recommendation and ops notes (quantization, memory needs, fallback plan)

Operational dependencies to flag to HealthGrid:
- If PHI testing required, we’ll need KMS/HSM integration and a Private deployment SLA (adds ~2–3 weeks)
- Network egress and IP allowlist for Redwood staging endpoints (HealthGrid infra)

I’ll upload the draft spreadsheet to the shared MAP link and mark the model rows with color-coded recommendations. Marissa — feel free to add any additional acceptance criteria you want surfaced to procurement.

-Rafael
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

---
Attachment: HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated with tradeoff snapshot)
